# Kayrock

Source: https://kayrock.hexdocs.pm/readme.md

# Kayrock

[![CI Checks](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/actions/workflows/checks.yml/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/actions/workflows/checks.yml)
[![CI Tests](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![Module Version](https://img.shields.io/hexpm/v/kayrock.svg)](https://hex.pm/packages/kayrock)
[![Hex Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/hex-docs-lightgreen.svg)](https://hexdocs.pm/kayrock/)
[![Total Download](https://img.shields.io/hexpm/dt/kayrock.svg)](https://hex.pm/packages/kayrock)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/hexpm/l/kayrock.svg)](https://hex.pm/packages/kayrock)
[![Last Updated](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/kafkaex/kayrock.svg)](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/commits/master)

Idiomatic Elixir interface to the Kafka protocol.

This library provides serialization and deserialization for all Kafka protocol messages,
based on [kafka_protocol](https://github.com/kafka4beam/kafka_protocol) for Erlang.
It is built to work with [KafkaEx](https://github.com/kafkaex/kafka_ex) though there
is no reason why it couldn't be used elsewhere.

## Installation

Add `kayrock` to your list of dependencies in `mix.exs`:

```elixir
def deps do
  [
    {:kayrock, "~> 1.0"}
  ]
end
```

## Requirements

- Elixir 1.14 or later
- Erlang/OTP 24.3 or later

## Basic Architecture and Usage

Kayrock generates structs for every version of every message in the Kafka
protocol. It does this by converting the Erlang-based schema descriptions in
`:kpro_schema` from the `kafka_protocol` library and is therefore limited to
messages and versions included there.

Each request message has a serializer (that generates iodata), and each response
message has a deserializer. There is also a protocol, `Kayrock.Request`, that has
an implementation created for each request.

The generated structs are namespaced as follows:
`Kayrock.<API>.V<version>.[Request|Response]`

For example:
- `Kayrock.Fetch.V4.Request`
- `Kayrock.Produce.V1.Response`
- `Kayrock.Metadata.V1.Request`

### Example Usage

```elixir
alias Kayrock.Request

# Create a request
request = %Kayrock.ApiVersions.V1.Request{
  client_id: "my_client",
  correlation_id: 0
}

# Serialize to wire protocol (iodata)
wire_protocol = Request.serialize(request)

# ... send wire_protocol over your connection ...
# ... receive binary response ...

# Deserialize the response
response_deserializer = Request.response_deserializer(request)
{deserialized_resp, _rest} = response_deserializer.(binary_response)

# deserialized_resp is now a %Kayrock.ApiVersions.V1.Response{}
```

## Message Compression

Kayrock supports four compression formats:

| Format | Built-in | Dependency Required |
|--------|----------|---------------------|
| gzip | Yes | None |
| snappy | No | `{:snappyer, "~> 1.2"}` |
| lz4 | No | `{:lz4b, "~> 0.0.13"}` |
| zstd | OTP 27+ | `{:ezstd, "~> 1.0"}` (for OTP < 27) |

### Installing Compression Dependencies

Add the compression libraries you need to your `mix.exs`:

```elixir
def deps do
  [
    {:kayrock, "~> 1.0"},

    # Add compression libraries as needed:
    {:snappyer, "~> 1.2"},     # For Snappy compression
    {:lz4b, "~> 0.0.13"},      # For LZ4 compression
    {:ezstd, "~> 1.0"},        # For Zstandard (OTP < 27)
  ]
end
```

### Zstandard Support

Zstandard compression is available via:
1. **OTP 27+**: Native `:zstd` module (no dependency needed)
2. **OTP < 27**: Add `{:ezstd, "~> 1.0"}` to your dependencies

## Code Generation

This repo includes a mix task, `mix gen.kafka_protocol`, that produces the code
in `lib/generated`. The generated code is checked into the repository to
simplify usage. End users should not need to run the mix task unless they are
doing development on Kayrock itself.

## Relationship to Other Libraries

Kayrock uses only the `kpro_schema` module from `kafka_protocol`.
`kafka_protocol` provides quite a lot of functionality (especially when used as
part of `brod`). This repo limits the integration surface because:

1. `kafka_protocol` produces Erlang records whereas Kayrock provides Elixir structs
2. `kafka_protocol` provides network-level implementation whereas Kayrock only
   provides serialization and deserialization
3. `kpro_schema` is itself automatically generated from the Java source code of
   Kafka, meaning that Kayrock could feasibly reproduce this without needing an
   intermediate dependency

### Built-in Client (Development Only)

This repo includes a lightweight Kafka client implementation for development and
testing purposes.

> **Warning:** The built-in client (`Kayrock.Client`) is NOT production-ready.
> For production usage, please use:
> - [KafkaEx](https://github.com/kafkaex/kafka_ex)
> - [brod](https://github.com/kafka4beam/brod)

## Testing

Kayrock includes both unit tests and integration tests.

### Unit Tests

```bash
mix test
```

### Integration Tests

Integration tests require Docker. We use
[testcontainers](https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-elixir)
to run a Kafka cluster.

```bash
# Requires Docker to be running
mix test.integration
```

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup and guidelines.

# Kayrock

Source: https://kayrock.hexdocs.pm/Kayrock.md

# `Kayrock`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/kayrock.ex#L1)

Idiomatic Elixir interface to the Kafka protocol.

Kayrock provides serialization and deserialization for all Kafka protocol
messages. It generates Elixir structs from the Kafka protocol schema,
allowing you to work with Kafka at the wire protocol level.

## Core Features

- Generated structs for every Kafka API version
- Serialization to wire protocol (iodata)
- Deserialization from binary responses
- Compression support (gzip, snappy, LZ4, Zstandard)

# `api_response`

```elixir
@type api_response() :: map()
```

Represents an API response message

This will generally be a generated struct.

# `api_version`

```elixir
@type api_version() :: non_neg_integer()
```

Specifies the version of an API message

Kayrock will generally try to pick a reasonable default here, but you can
override it in many cases.  See [Kafka Protocol Documentation](https://kafka.apache.org/protocol.html#The_Messages_Metadata)

# `broker_pid`

```elixir
@type broker_pid() :: pid()
```

A `pid` for a `Kayrock.BrokerConnection` process.

This is for low-level communication with individual brokers.  Generally you
should work with a `client_pid`.

# `client_pid`

```elixir
@type client_pid() :: pid()
```

A `pid` for a `Kayrock.Client` process.

# `node_id`

```elixir
@type node_id() :: integer()
```

A broker's advertised integer node id

# `node_selector`

```elixir
@type node_selector() ::
  node_id()
  | :random
  | :controller
  | {:topic_partition, topic_name(), partition_id()}
```

A node selector for sending messages to the cluster

Generally the Kayrock API will select the right node depending on the
operation.  These are exposed to provide fine-grained user control in a few
cases where it might make sense to override the default.

Possible values:
* Integer - Directly access a node by id.  Generally you should not do this
  unless you are operating at a low level.
* `:random` - Select a node at random from the cluster metadata.
* `:controller` - Select the controller node - this is used for cluster
  management messages

# `partition_id`

```elixir
@type partition_id() :: non_neg_integer()
```

# `topic_name`

```elixir
@type topic_name() :: binary()
```

# `api_versions`

```elixir
@spec api_versions(client_pid(), api_version(), node_selector()) ::
  {:ok, api_response()}
```

Fetch the supported API versions from the cluster
Kayrock currently supports versions 0 and 1.
[ApiVersions](https://kafka.apache.org/protocol.html#The_Messages_ApiVersions)

# `broker_sync_call`

```elixir
@spec broker_sync_call(pid(), Kayrock.Request.t()) :: {:ok, map()} | {:error, term()}
```

Makes a synchronous call directly to a broker

`broker_id` should be the pid of a `Kayrock.BrokerConnection`.  `request` must
have an implementation for the `Kayrock.Request` protocol.

# `client_call`

```elixir
@spec client_call(client_pid(), Kayrock.Request.t(), node_selector()) ::
  {:ok, api_response()}
```

Make an api call to a Kafka cluster mediated through a client

# `create_topics`

Create one or more topics

# `delete_topics`

Delete topics from the Kafka cluster.

# `fetch`

Fetch messages from a Kafka topic.

## Options

- `:version` - Protocol version to use (default: 4)
- `:max_wait_time` - Maximum wait time in ms (default: 1000)
- `:min_bytes` - Minimum bytes to return (default: 0)
- `:max_bytes` - Maximum bytes to return (default: 1_000_000)
- `:isolation_level` - 0 = read uncommitted, 1 = read committed (default: 1)

# `produce`

# `produce`

Produce messages to a Kafka topic.

## Options

- `:version` - Protocol version to use (default: 1)
- `:acks` - Acknowledgment level (default: -1 for all replicas)
- `:timeout` - Request timeout in ms (default: 1000)

# `topics_metadata`

Fetch metadata for topics from the Kafka cluster.

## Parameters

- `client_pid` - PID of a `Kayrock.Client` process
- `topics` - List of topic names, or `nil` for all topics

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

# Kayrock.AddOffsetsToTxn

Source: https://kayrock.hexdocs.pm/Kayrock.AddOffsetsToTxn.md

# `Kayrock.AddOffsetsToTxn`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/add_offsets_to_txn.ex#L1)

Kayrock-generated module for the Kafka `add_offsets_to_txn` API

# `request_t`

```elixir
@type request_t() ::
  Kayrock.AddOffsetsToTxn.V1.Request.t()
  | Kayrock.AddOffsetsToTxn.V0.Request.t()
```

Union type for all request structs for this API

# `response_t`

```elixir
@type response_t() ::
  Kayrock.AddOffsetsToTxn.V1.Response.t()
  | Kayrock.AddOffsetsToTxn.V0.Response.t()
```

Union type for all response structs for this API

# `deserialize`

```elixir
@spec deserialize(integer(), binary()) :: {response_t(), binary()}
```

Deserializes raw wire data for this API with the given version

# `get_request_struct`

```elixir
@spec get_request_struct(integer()) :: request_t()
```

Returns a request struct for this API with the given version

# `max_vsn`

```elixir
@spec max_vsn() :: integer()
```

Returns the maximum version of this API supported by Kayrock (1)

# `min_vsn`

```elixir
@spec min_vsn() :: integer()
```

Returns the minimum version of this API supported by Kayrock (0)

# Kayrock.AddOffsetsToTxn.V0.Request

Source: https://kayrock.hexdocs.pm/Kayrock.AddOffsetsToTxn.V0.Request.md

# `Kayrock.AddOffsetsToTxn.V0.Request`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/add_offsets_to_txn.ex#L12)

Kayrock-generated request struct for Kafka `add_offsets_to_txn` v0 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  transactional_id: :string,
  producer_id: :int64,
  producer_epoch: :int16,
  group_id: :string
]
```

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %Kayrock.AddOffsetsToTxn.V0.Request{
  client_id: nil | binary(),
  correlation_id: nil | integer(),
  group_id: nil | binary(),
  producer_epoch: nil | integer(),
  producer_id: nil | integer(),
  transactional_id: nil | binary()
}
```

Request struct for the Kafka `add_offsets_to_txn` API v0

# `api_key`

```elixir
@spec api_key() :: integer()
```

Returns the Kafka API key for this API

# `api_vsn`

```elixir
@spec api_vsn() :: integer()
```

Returns the API version (0) implemented by this module

# `response_deserializer`

```elixir
@spec response_deserializer() :: (binary() -&gt;
                              {Kayrock.AddOffsetsToTxn.V0.Response.t(),
                               binary()})
```

Returns a function that can be used to deserialize the wire response from the
broker for this message type

# `schema`

```elixir
@spec schema() :: term()
```

Returns the schema of this message

See [above](#).

# `serialize`

```elixir
@spec serialize(t()) :: iodata()
```

Serialize a message to binary data for transfer to a Kafka broker

```elixir
  correlation_id: nil | integer(),
  producer_epoch: nil | integer(),
  producer_id: nil | integer(),
```
```elixir
  topics: [%{topic: nil | binary(), partitions: [nil | integer()]}],
  transactional_id: nil | binary()
}
```

# Kayrock.AddPartitionsToTxn.V1.Response

Source: https://kayrock.hexdocs.pm/Kayrock.AddPartitionsToTxn.V1.Response.md

# `Kayrock.AddPartitionsToTxn.V1.Response`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/add_partitions_to_txn.ex#L384)

Kayrock-generated response struct for Kafka `add_partitions_to_txn` v1 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  throttle_time_ms: :int32,
  errors: {:array,
   [
     topic: :string,
     partition_errors: {:array, [partition: :int32, error_code: :int16]}
   ]}
]
```

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %Kayrock.AddPartitionsToTxn.V1.Response{
  correlation_id: integer(),
  errors: [
    %{
      topic: nil | binary(),
      partition_errors: [
        %{partition: nil | integer(), error_code: nil | integer()}
      ]
    }
  ],
  throttle_time_ms: nil | integer()
}
```

Response struct for the Kafka `add_partitions_to_txn` API v1

```
]
```

```elixir
          name: nil | binary(),
```

# `Kayrock.Client`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/kayrock/client.ex#L1)

Development client for communicating with a Kafka cluster.

## Limitations

This client lacks:
- Connection pooling
- Proper supervision tree
- Circuit breaker patterns
- Automatic reconnection handling
- Production-grade error handling
- Telemetry/monitoring

# Kayrock.Compression

Source: https://kayrock.hexdocs.pm/Kayrock.Compression.md

# `Kayrock.Compression`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/kayrock/compression.ex#L1)

Handles compression/decompression of messages.

See https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/KAFKA/A+Guide+To+The+Kafka+Protocol#AGuideToTheKafkaProtocol-Compression

To add new compression types:

1. Add the appropriate dependency to mix.exs (don't forget to add it
to the application list).
2. Add the appropriate attribute value and compression_type atom.
3. Add new Compression module.
4. Add a decompress function in the new module.
5. Add a compress function in the new module.

## Compression Levels

- **Gzip**: 1 (fastest) to 9 (best compression), default: 6
- **Zstandard**: 1 (fastest) to 22 (best compression), default: 3
- **Snappy/LZ4**: No levels supported

## Dependencies

- **Snappy**: `{:snappyer, "~> 1.2"}`
- **LZ4**: `{:lz4b, "~> 0.2.0"}`
- **Zstandard**: `{:ezstd, "~> 1.0"}`

## Zstandard (zstd) Requirements

Zstandard compression (codec 4) requires:
- Produce API version 7 or later (corresponds to KAFKA_2_1_IV0+)
- Kafka broker version 2.1.0 or later
- RecordBatch format (message format v2)

If you use an older Produce API version (v0-v6), you'll receive error code 76
(UNSUPPORTED_COMPRESSION_TYPE). The Confluent Kafka container includes zstd-jni
support by default.

# `codec_t`

```elixir
@type codec_t() :: :gzip | :snappy | :lz4 | :zstd
```

# `available_codecs`

```elixir
@spec available_codecs() :: [codec_t()]
```

# `compress`

# `compress`

# `decompress`

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# `t`


```
        tagged_fields: :tagged_fields

     tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
```
```
   ]},
```

```
  validate_only: :boolean,
```

[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/create_topics.ex#L1537)

Kayrock-generated response struct for Kafka `create_topics` v5 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  throttle_time_ms: :int32,
  topics: {:compact_array,
   [
     name: :compact_string,
     error_code: :int16,
     error_message: :compact_nullable_string,
     num_partitions: :int32,
     replication_factor: :int16,
     configs: {:compact_array,
      [
        name: :compact_string,
        value: :compact_nullable_string,
        read_only: :boolean,
        config_source: :int8,
        is_sensitive: :boolean,
        tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
      ]},
     tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
   ]},
  tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
]
```

```elixir
    nil
    | [
        %{
          name: nil | binary(),
          error_code: nil | integer(),
          error_message: nil | binary(),
          num_partitions: nil | integer(),
          replication_factor: nil | integer(),
          configs:
            nil
            | [
                %{
                  name: nil | binary(),
                  value: nil | binary(),
                  read_only: nil | integer(),
                  config_source: nil | integer(),
                  is_sensitive: nil | integer(),
                  tagged_fields: [{non_neg_integer(), binary()}]
                }
              ],
          tagged_fields: [{non_neg_integer(), binary()}]
        }
      ]
}
```

```
     tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
```

```elixir
          partition_id: nil | integer(),
          error_code: nil | integer(),
          error_message: nil | binary()
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  throttle_time_ms: nil | integer()
}
```

Response struct for the Kafka `elect_leaders` API v1

# `Kayrock.ElectLeaders.V2.Response`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/elect_leaders.ex#L713)

Kayrock-generated response struct for Kafka `elect_leaders` v2 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  throttle_time_ms: :int32,
  error_code: :int16,
  replica_election_results: {:compact_array,
   [
     topic: :compact_string,
     partition_result: {:compact_array,
      [
        partition_id: :int32,
        error_code: :int16,
        error_message: :compact_nullable_string,
        tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
      ]},
     tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
   ]},
  tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
]
```

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %Kayrock.ElectLeaders.V2.Response{
  correlation_id: integer(),
  error_code: nil | integer(),
  replica_election_results:
    nil
    | [
        %{
          topic: nil | binary(),
          partition_result:
            nil
            | [
                %{
                  partition_id: nil | integer(),
                  error_code: nil | integer(),
                  error_message: nil | binary(),
                  tagged_fields: [{non_neg_integer(), binary()}]
                }
              ],
          tagged_fields: [{non_neg_integer(), binary()}]
        }
      ],
  tagged_fields: [{non_neg_integer(), binary()}],
  throttle_time_ms: nil | integer()
}
```

Response struct for the Kafka `elect_leaders` API v2

# Kayrock.ErrorCode

Source: https://kayrock.hexdocs.pm/Kayrock.ErrorCode.md

# `Kayrock.ErrorCode`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/kayrock/error_code.ex#L1)

Utility for converting Kafka error codes to/from atom names

Note the actual error code values are determined by `:kpro_schema.c/1` for codes -1 to 71.
Extended error codes (72-119) are defined locally to support newer Kafka versions.

See https://kafka.apache.org/protocol#protocol_error_codes

# `error_atom`

```elixir
@type error_atom() :: atom()
```

An erlang/elixir atom representation of an error code

# `error_code`

```elixir
@type error_code() :: integer()
```

A numeric Kafka error code

# `atom_to_code`

```elixir
@spec atom_to_code(error_atom()) :: error_code() | nil
```

Converts an atom to a numeric error code

Returns nil if an unknown atom is supplied

# `atom_to_code!`

```elixir
@spec atom_to_code!(error_atom()) :: error_code()
```

Converts an atom to a numeric error code, raising an
`Kayrock.ErrorCode.InvalidAtomException` if an unknown atom is supplied

# `code_to_atom`

```elixir
@spec code_to_atom(error_code()) :: error_atom()
```

Converts an error code to an atom

An unknown code results in a return of `:unknown`

# `code_to_atom!`

```elixir
@spec code_to_atom!(error_code()) :: error_atom()
```

Converts an error code to an atom, raising an
`Kayrock.ErrorCode.InvalidErrorCodeException` if an unknown error code is supplied

# `unknown_topic`

```elixir
@spec unknown_topic() :: error_code()
```

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/fetch.ex#L12)

Kayrock-generated request struct for Kafka `fetch` v0 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  replica_id: :int32,
  max_wait_time: :int32,
  min_bytes: :int32,
  topics: {:array,
   [
     topic: :string,
     partitions: {:array,
      [partition: :int32, fetch_offset: :int64, partition_max_bytes: :int32]}
   ]}
]
```

messages

```
          error_code: :int16,
          high_watermark: :int64
        ],
        record_set: :records
      ]}
   ]}
```

# `Kayrock.Fetch.V10.Request`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/fetch.ex#L1922)

Kayrock-generated request struct for Kafka `fetch` v10 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  replica_id: :int32,
  max_wait_time: :int32,
  min_bytes: :int32,
  max_bytes: :int32,
  isolation_level: :int8,
  session_id: :int32,
  session_epoch: :int32,
  topics: {:array,
   [
     topic: :string,
     partitions: {:array,
      [
        partition: :int32,
        current_leader_epoch: :int32,
        fetch_offset: :int64,
        log_start_offset: :int64,
        partition_max_bytes: :int32
      ]}
   ]},
  forgotten_topics_data: {:array,
   [
     topic: :string,
     partitions: {:array,
      [
        partition: :int32,
        current_leader_epoch: :int32,
        fetch_offset: :int64,
        log_start_offset: :int64,
        partition_max_bytes: :int32

   ]}
```

```
          error_code: :int16,
          high_watermark: :int64,
          last_stable_offset: :int64,
          log_start_offset: :int64,
          aborted_transactions: {:array,
```

# Kayrock.Fetch.V8.Response

Source: https://kayrock.hexdocs.pm/Kayrock.Fetch.V8.Response.md

# `Kayrock.Fetch.V8.Response`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/fetch.ex#L4186)

Kayrock-generated response struct for Kafka `fetch` v8 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  throttle_time_ms: :int32,
  error_code: :int16,
  session_id: :int32,
  responses: {:array,
   [
     topic: :string,
     partition_responses: {:array,
      [
        partition_header: [
          partition: :int32,
          error_code: :int16,
          high_watermark: :int64,
          last_stable_offset: :int64,
          log_start_offset: :int64,
          aborted_transactions: {:array,
           [producer_id: :int64, first_offset: :int64]}
        ],
        record_set: :records
      ]}
   ]}
]
```

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %Kayrock.Fetch.V8.Response{
  correlation_id: integer(),
  error_code: nil | integer(),
  responses: [
    %{
      topic: nil | binary(),
      partition_responses: [
        %{
          partition_header: %{
            partition: nil | integer(),
            error_code: nil | integer(),
            high_watermark: nil | integer(),
            last_stable_offset: nil | integer(),
            log_start_offset: nil | integer(),
            aborted_transactions: [
              %{producer_id: nil | integer(), first_offset: nil | integer()}
            ]
          },
          record_set: nil | Kayrock.MessageSet.t() | Kayrock.RecordBatch.t()
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  session_id: nil | integer(),
  throttle_time_ms: nil | integer()
}
```

Response struct for the Kafka `fetch` API v8

# Kayrock.Fetch.V9.Request

Source: https://kayrock.hexdocs.pm/Kayrock.Fetch.V9.Request.md

# `Kayrock.Fetch.V9.Request`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/fetch.ex#L1660)

Kayrock-generated request struct for Kafka `fetch` v9 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  replica_id: :int32,
  max_wait_time: :int32,
  min_bytes: :int32,
  max_bytes: :int32,
  isolation_level: :int8,
  session_id: :int32,
  session_epoch: :int32,
  topics: {:array,
   [
     topic: :string,
     partitions: {:array,
      [
        partition: :int32,
        current_leader_epoch: :int32,
        fetch_offset: :int64,
        log_start_offset: :int64,
        partition_max_bytes: :int32
      ]}
   ]},
  forgotten_topics_data: {:array,
   [
     topic: :string,
     partitions: {:array,
      [
        partition: :int32,
        current_leader_epoch: :int32,
        fetch_offset: :int64,
        log_start_offset: :int64,
        partition_max_bytes: :int32
      ]}
   ]}
]
```

```elixir
          current_leader_epoch: nil | integer(),
          fetch_offset: nil | integer(),
          log_start_offset: nil | integer(),
          partition_max_bytes: nil | integer()
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  isolation_level: nil | integer(),
  max_bytes: nil | integer(),
  max_wait_time: nil | integer(),
  min_bytes: nil | integer(),
  replica_id: nil | integer(),
  session_epoch: nil | integer(),
  session_id: nil | integer(),
  topics: [
    %{
      topic: nil | binary(),
      partitions: [
        %{
          partition: nil | integer(),
          current_leader_epoch: nil | integer(),
          fetch_offset: nil | integer(),
          log_start_offset: nil | integer(),
          partition_max_bytes: nil | integer()
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

messages

```
[
```

```
  session_timeout_ms: :int32,
  rebalance_timeout_ms: :int32,
  member_id: :compact_string,
  group_instance_id: :compact_nullable_string,
  protocol_type: :compact_string,
  protocols: {:compact_array,
   [
     name: :compact_string,
     metadata: :compact_bytes,
     tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
   ]},
  tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
]
```

```elixir
  correlation_id: nil | integer(),

  member_id: nil | binary(),
  protocol_type: nil | binary(),
  protocols:
    nil
    | [
        %{
          name: nil | binary(),
          metadata: nil | binary(),
          tagged_fields: [{non_neg_integer(), binary()}]
        }
      ],
  rebalance_timeout_ms: nil | integer(),
  session_timeout_ms: nil | integer(),
  tagged_fields: [{non_neg_integer(), binary()}]
}
```

# Kayrock.ListOffsets.V0.Request

# `Kayrock.ListOffsets.V0.Request`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/list_offsets.ex#L12)

Kayrock-generated request struct for Kafka `list_offsets` v0 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  replica_id: :int32,
  topics: {:array,
   [
     topic: :string,
     partitions: {:array,
      [partition: :int32, timestamp: :int64, max_num_offsets: :int32]}
   ]}
]
```

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %Kayrock.ListOffsets.V0.Request{
  client_id: nil | binary(),
  correlation_id: nil | integer(),
  replica_id: nil | integer(),
  topics: [
    %{
```

messages

```
[
  throttle_time_ms: :int32,
  error_code: :int16,
  error_message: :compact_nullable_string,
  topics: {:compact_array,
   [
     name: :compact_string,
     partitions: {:compact_array,
      [
        partition_index: :int32,
        replicas: {:compact_array, :int32},
        adding_replicas: {:compact_array, :int32},
        removing_replicas: {:compact_array, :int32},
        tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
      ]},
     tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
   ]},
  tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
]
```

```elixir
  throttle_time_ms: nil | integer(),

    nil
    | [
        %{
          name: nil | binary(),
          partitions:
            nil
            | [
                %{
                  partition_index: nil | integer(),
                  replicas: nil | [nil | integer()],
                  adding_replicas: nil | [nil | integer()],
                  removing_replicas: nil | [nil | integer()],
                  tagged_fields: [{non_neg_integer(), binary()}]
                }
              ],
          tagged_fields: [{non_neg_integer(), binary()}]
        }
      ]
}
```

# Kayrock.Macros

Source: https://kayrock.hexdocs.pm/Kayrock.Macros.md

# `Kayrock.Macros`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/kayrock/macros.ex#L1)

Useful macros for kafka-related values

`use Kayrock.Macros` is a convenient way to use these

# `earliest_offset`
*macro* 

Timestamp to supply for the earliest offset

# `full_isr_acks`
*macro* 

Full ISR acks required on produce

# `latest_offset`
*macro* 

Timestamp to supply for the latest offset

# `leader_ack`
*macro* 

Only leader ack required on produce

# `no_acks`
*macro* 

No acks required on produce

# `no_error`
*macro* 

The error code value indicating no error

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

```
     rack: :compact_nullable_string,
     tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
   ]},

  controller_id: :int32,
  topics: {:compact_array,
   [
     error_code: :int16,
     name: :compact_string,
     is_internal: :boolean,

        leader_epoch: :int32,

        isr_nodes: {:compact_array, :int32},

      ]},
     topic_authorized_operations: :int32,
     tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
```

```elixir
          error_code: nil | integer(),

            nil
            | [
                %{
                  error_code: nil | integer(),
                  partition_index: nil | integer(),
                  leader_id: nil | integer(),
                  leader_epoch: nil | integer(),
                  replica_nodes: nil | [nil | integer()],
                  isr_nodes: nil | [nil | integer()],
                  offline_replicas: nil | [nil | integer()],
                  tagged_fields: [{non_neg_integer(), binary()}]
                }
              ],
          topic_authorized_operations: nil | integer(),
          tagged_fields: [{non_neg_integer(), binary()}]
        }
      ]
}
```

Response struct for the Kafka `metadata` API v9

messages

```
[
```

```
  topic_data: {:array,
   [topic: :string, data: {:array, [partition: :int32, record_set: :records]}]}
]
```

```elixir
    %{
      topic: nil | binary(),
      data: [
        %{
          partition: nil | integer(),
          record_set: nil | Kayrock.MessageSet.t() | Kayrock.RecordBatch.t()
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/produce.ex#L1614)

Kayrock-generated response struct for Kafka `produce` v2 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  responses: {:array,
   [
     topic: :string,
     partition_responses: {:array,
      [
        partition: :int32,
        error_code: :int16,
        base_offset: :int64,
        log_append_time: :int64
      ]}
   ]},
  throttle_time_ms: :int32
]
```

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %Kayrock.Produce.V2.Response{
  correlation_id: integer(),
  responses: [
    %{
      topic: nil | binary(),
      partition_responses: [
        %{
          partition: nil | integer(),
          error_code: nil | integer(),
          base_offset: nil | integer(),
          log_append_time: nil | integer()
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  throttle_time_ms: nil | integer()
}
```

Response struct for the Kafka `produce` API v2

# `api_key`

```elixir
@spec api_key() :: integer()
```

Returns the Kafka API key for this API

# `Kayrock.Produce.V3.Request`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/produce.ex#L420)

Kayrock-generated request struct for Kafka `produce` v3 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  transactional_id: :nullable_string,
  acks: :int16,
  timeout: :int32,
  topic_data: {:array,
   [topic: :string, data: {:array, [partition: :int32, record_set: :records]}]}
]
```

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %Kayrock.Produce.V3.Request{
  acks: nil | integer(),
  client_id: nil | binary(),
  correlation_id: nil | integer(),
  timeout: nil | integer(),
  topic_data: [
    %{
      topic: nil | binary(),
      data: [
        %{
          partition: nil | integer(),
          record_set: nil | Kayrock.MessageSet.t() | Kayrock.RecordBatch.t()
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  transactional_id: nil | binary()
}
```

Request struct for the Kafka `produce` API v3

```elixir
@spec api_key() :: integer()
```

# Kayrock.Produce.V8.Response

Source: https://kayrock.hexdocs.pm/Kayrock.Produce.V8.Response.md

# `Kayrock.Produce.V8.Response`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/produce.ex#L2619)

Kayrock-generated response struct for Kafka `produce` v8 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  responses: {:array,
   [
     topic: :string,
     partition_responses: {:array,
      [
        partition: :int32,
        error_code: :int16,
        base_offset: :int64,
        log_append_time: :int64,
        log_start_offset: :int64,
        record_errors: {:array,
         [batch_index: :int32, batch_index_error_message: :nullable_string]},
        error_message: :nullable_string
      ]}
   ]},
  throttle_time_ms: :int32
]
```

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %Kayrock.Produce.V8.Response{
  correlation_id: integer(),
  responses: [
    %{
      topic: nil | binary(),
      partition_responses: [
        %{
          partition: nil | integer(),
          error_code: nil | integer(),
          base_offset: nil | integer(),
          log_append_time: nil | integer(),
          log_start_offset: nil | integer(),
          record_errors: [
            %{
              batch_index: nil | integer(),
              batch_index_error_message: nil | binary()
            }
          ],
          error_message: nil | binary()
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  throttle_time_ms: nil | integer()
}
```

Response struct for the Kafka `produce` API v8

# `api_key`

```elixir
@spec api_key() :: integer()
```

Returns the Kafka API key for this API

# `api_vsn`

```elixir
@spec api_vsn() :: integer()
```

Returns the API version (8) implemented by this module

```elixir
@spec deserialize(binary()) :: {t(), binary()}
```

# Kayrock.RecordBatch

Source: https://kayrock.hexdocs.pm/Kayrock.RecordBatch.md

# `Kayrock.RecordBatch`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/kayrock/record_batch.ex#L1)

Represents a batch of records (also called a record set)

This is the newer format in Kafka 0.11+

See https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/#recordbatch

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %Kayrock.RecordBatch{
  attributes: term(),
  base_sequence: term(),
  batch_length: term(),
  batch_offset: term(),
  crc: term(),
  first_timestamp: term(),
  last_offset_delta: term(),
  max_timestamp: term(),
  partition_leader_epoch: term(),
  producer_epoch: term(),
  producer_id: term(),
  records: term()
}
```

# `deserialize`

```elixir
@spec deserialize(binary()) :: nil | Kayrock.MessageSet.t() | t()
```

Direct deserializer
Supplied for compatibility with the Request protocol

# `deserialize`

```elixir
@spec deserialize(integer(), binary()) :: nil | Kayrock.MessageSet.t() | t()
```

# `from_binary_list`

```elixir
@spec from_binary_list([binary()], atom()) :: t()
```

# `serialize`

```elixir
@spec serialize(t()) :: iodata()
```

# Kayrock.Socket

Source: https://kayrock.hexdocs.pm/Kayrock.Socket.md

# `Kayrock.Socket`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/kayrock/socket.ex#L1)

This module handle all socket related operations.

NOTE this is a copy of KafkaEx.Socket:
https://github.com/kafkaex/kafka_ex/blob/master/lib/kafka_ex/socket.ex

It is duplicated here to avoid creating a circular dependency.

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %Kayrock.Socket{
  socket: :gen_tcp.socket() | :ssl.sslsocket(),
  ssl: boolean()
}
```

# `close`

```elixir
@spec close(t()) :: :ok
```

Closes the socket.

For more information, see `:ssl.close/1` for ssl or `:gen_tcp.send/1` for non ssl.

# `create`

Creates a socket.

For more information about the available options, see `:ssl.connect/3` for ssl
or `:gen_tcp.connect/3` for non ssl.

# `info`

```elixir
@spec info(t()) :: list() | nil
```

Returns the information about the socket.

For more information, see `Port.info`

# `open?`

```elixir
@spec open?(t()) :: boolean()
```

Returns true if the socket is open

# `recv`

```elixir
@spec recv(t(), non_neg_integer()) ::
  {:ok, String.t() | binary() | term()} | {:error, any()}
```

Receives data from the socket.

For more information, see `:ssl.recv/2` for ssl or `:gen_tcp.recv/2` for non ssl.

# `recv`

```elixir
@spec recv(t(), non_neg_integer(), timeout()) ::
  {:ok, String.t() | binary() | term()} | {:error, any()}
```

# `send`

```elixir
@spec send(t(), iodata()) :: :ok | {:error, any()}
```

Sends data over the socket.

It handles both, SSL and non SSL sockets.

For more information, see `:ssl.send/2` for ssl or `:gen_tcp.send/2` for non ssl.

# `setopts`

```elixir
@spec setopts(t(), list()) :: :ok | {:error, any()}
```

Set options to the socket.

For more information, see `:ssl.setopts/2` for ssl or `:inet.setopts/2` for non ssl.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# `Kayrock.SyncGroup.V4.Request`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/sync_group.ex#L525)

Kayrock-generated request struct for Kafka `sync_group` v4 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  group_id: :compact_string,
  generation_id: :int32,
  member_id: :compact_string,
  group_instance_id: :compact_nullable_string,
  assignments: {:compact_array,
   [
     member_id: :compact_string,
     assignment: :compact_bytes,
     tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
   ]},
  tagged_fields: :tagged_fields
]
```

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %Kayrock.SyncGroup.V4.Request{
  assignments:
    nil
    | [
        %{
          member_id: nil | binary(),
          assignment: nil | binary(),
          tagged_fields: [{non_neg_integer(), binary()}]
        }
      ],
  client_id: nil | binary(),
  correlation_id: nil | integer(),
  generation_id: nil | integer(),
  group_id: nil | binary(),
  group_instance_id: nil | binary(),
  member_id: nil | binary(),
  tagged_fields: [{non_neg_integer(), binary()}]
}
```

# Kayrock.TxnOffsetCommit.V0.Request

Source: https://kayrock.hexdocs.pm/Kayrock.TxnOffsetCommit.V0.Request.md

# `Kayrock.TxnOffsetCommit.V0.Request`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/txn_offset_commit.ex#L12)

Kayrock-generated request struct for Kafka `txn_offset_commit` v0 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  transactional_id: :string,
  group_id: :string,
  producer_id: :int64,
  producer_epoch: :int16,
  topics: {:array,
   [
     name: :string,
     partitions: {:array,
      [
        partition_index: :int32,
        committed_offset: :int64,
        committed_metadata: :nullable_string
      ]}
   ]}
]
```

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %Kayrock.TxnOffsetCommit.V0.Request{
  client_id: nil | binary(),
  correlation_id: nil | integer(),
  group_id: nil | binary(),
  producer_epoch: nil | integer(),
  producer_id: nil | integer(),
  topics: [
    %{
      name: nil | binary(),
      partitions: [
        %{
          partition_index: nil | integer(),
          committed_offset: nil | integer(),
          committed_metadata: nil | binary()
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  transactional_id: nil | binary()
}
```

Request struct for the Kafka `txn_offset_commit` API v0

# `api_key`

```elixir
@spec api_key() :: integer()
```

Returns the Kafka API key for this API

# `api_vsn`

```elixir
@spec api_vsn() :: integer()
```

Returns the API version (0) implemented by this module

# `response_deserializer`

```elixir
@spec response_deserializer() :: (binary() -&gt;
                              {Kayrock.TxnOffsetCommit.V0.Response.t(),
                               binary()})
```

Returns a function that can be used to deserialize the wire response from the
broker for this message type

# `schema`

```elixir
@spec schema() :: term()
```

Returns the schema of this message

# `Kayrock.TxnOffsetCommit.V0.Response`
[🔗](https://github.com/kafkaex/kayrock/blob/main/lib/generated/txn_offset_commit.ex#L531)

Kayrock-generated response struct for Kafka `txn_offset_commit` v0 API
messages

The schema of this API is
```
[
  throttle_time_ms: :int32,
  topics: {:array,
   [
     name: :string,
     partitions: {:array, [partition_index: :int32, error_code: :int16]}
   ]}
]
```

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %Kayrock.TxnOffsetCommit.V0.Response{
  correlation_id: integer(),
  throttle_time_ms: nil | integer(),
  topics: [
    %{
      name: nil | binary(),
      partitions: [
        %{partition_index: nil | integer(), error_code: nil | integer()}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Response struct for the Kafka `txn_offset_commit` API v0
